title: Strength Training During Pregnancy: The Trial MOVE4TWO
official: Effects of Strength Training During Pregnancy on Maternal and Fetal Health: A Randomized Controlled Trial
summary:
Pregnancy involves substantial physiological and psychological adaptations that may affect maternal health, physical function, and quality of life. Regular physical activity during pregnancy has been associated with improvements in physical and psychological well-being and a reduced risk of certain pregnancy-related complications. Although aerobic exercise is widely recommended, the specific effects of structured strength training on maternal functional capacity, neuromuscular performance, cardiovascular function, and fetal health remain insufficiently understood.

The aim of this randomized controlled trial is to evaluate the effects of a supervised strength training program during pregnancy on maternal health-related quality of life, physical fitness, body composition, physiological biomarkers, fetal growth, and perinatal outcomes in healthy pregnant women.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Primigravid women with a singleton pregnancy.
* Age between 20 and 35 years.
* Pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI) below 30 kg/m².
* Medical clearance to participate in supervised exercise.
* Absence of pregnancy-related conditions, including gestational diabetes, preeclampsia, or gestational hypertension.
* Availability to attend three supervised training sessions per week (approximately 60 minutes per session).

Exclusion Criteria:

* Musculoskeletal injury within six months before the baseline assessment.
* Major surgery within the previous three months.
* Any absolute or relative contraindication to exercise identified using the PARmed-X for Pregnancy questionnaire, including relevant obstetric, cardiovascular, respiratory, or systemic conditions.
* Any other medical condition that contraindicates participation in supervised physical activity.
* High-risk pregnancy.
